Let me analyze this OIML certificate for a water meter.

Key facts:
- Certificate number: R49/2013-A-NL1-21.04 revision 5
- Scheme: A
- Project number: 4074653
- Page total: 4
- Member state: The Netherlands
- Date issued: 31 August 2026
- OIML issuer ID: NL1 (NMi Certin B.V., OIML Issuing Authority NL1)

- Person responsible: M.Ph.D. Schmidt
- Title: Certification Board (not exactly a title... "Certification Board" appears after the date — likely the person signs on behalf of the Certification Board). I'll put person_title: "Certification Board" — hmm, it's a bit ambiguous but it's what's in the document.
- Phone: +31 88 636 2332
- Email: certin@nmi.nl

Certified type:
- Category: "Water meter" — the schema examples list "Gas meter" etc. This is an ultrasonic water meter. Category: "Water meter"
- Type designations: ["E-Series G2®"]
- Module designation: null or "Not applicable" — not mentioned; omit or null.
- Description: "An ultrasonic water meter"

Recommendation:
- id: "R49"
- edition: 2013
- amendment: null
- scheme: "A"
- accuracy_classes: ["2"]

Test reports:
- NMi-2284950-01 dated 11 June 2021, 120 pages, role: type_evaluation_report? The text says "the results of tests and examinations provided in the associated reports". Hard to tell roles. The first (dated at initial issue) is likely the Type Evaluation Report. Others are additional test reports related to revisions. I'll assign:
  - NMi-2284950-01: 11 June 2021, 120 pages, role: type_evaluation_report
  - NMi-2619384-01: 21 January 2022, 70 pages, role: test_report
  - NMi-4020293-01: 13 April 2026, 12 pages, role: test_report
  - NMi-4074653-01: 31 August 2026, 17 pages, role: test_report (matches project number; could be evaluation report)
  
Hmm, NMi-4074653-01 has the project number prefix, so it might be the evaluation report for this revision. I'll use "evaluation_report" for that one. Actually to be safe: the schema roles include type_evaluation_report | test_report | documentation_file | evaluation_report. Also documentation folder number T12126-5 is a documentation file. Should I add that as test_reports entry with role documentation_file? The rule says test_reports[] with role documentation_file. The construction is "recorded in documentation folder number T12126-5". I'll include it: id "T12126-5", role "documentation_file", no date/pages.

Revision history:
- 0, 11 June 2021, Initial issue.
- 1, 21 January 2022, Increasing flow rate ratio Q3/Q1 to R800 due to revised element insert
- 2, 2 September 2022, ASIC firmware update to support alternate pressure transducer
- 3, 1 April 2025, Documentation folder update
- 4, 13 April 2026, Addition of reflector material 90/10 COPPER-NICKEL, C70600
- 5, 31 August 2026, Changes of PCBA

Footnotes:
- "1)" The measurement sensor with element insert according to documentation number 12126/0-05
- "2)" The measurement sensor with element insert according to documentation number 12126/1-01 and 12126/4-04.

Also the asterisk footnotes from Table 2:
- "*": Only the lower 16-bits of the 32-bit calculations is displayed as stated in bold.
- "**": Two checksums are possible depending on the memory section used at that time.

Model family: Table 3 shows meter sizes DN15 and DN20, with two variants each (footnote 1 and 2, i.e., different element inserts). So models: DN15 (variant 1), DN20 (variant 1), DN15 (variant 2), DN20 (variant 2). 

Flow rates:
- DN15¹: Q1=0.0063, Q2=0.01, Q3=2.5, Q4=3.125, Q3/Q1=400
- DN20¹: Q1=0.01, Q2=0.016, Q3=4, Q4=5, Q3/Q1=400
- DN15²: Q1=0.0031, Q2=0.005, Q3=2.5, Q4=3.125, Q3/Q1=800
- DN20²: Q1=0.005, Q2=0.008, Q3=4, Q4=5, Q3/Q1=800

Model IDs: I'll use "DN15 (insert 12126/0-05)" style or "DN15-R400"? Better to keep with footnotes: model_id: "DN15^1" ... Let me use "DN15 (variant 1)" and "DN15 (variant 2)"? Or incorporate footnote: model_id "DN15¹". JSON supports unicode superscripts. Let me use "DN15 (element insert 12126/0-05)" and "DN15 (element insert 12126/1-01 & 12126/4-04)". Simpler: "DN15-R400" and "DN15-R800" based on Q3/Q1 ratio. Actually the distinguishing attribute is the Q3/Q1 ratio (400 vs 800) which corresponds to element insert. The revision history says "Increasing flow rate ratio Q3/Q1 to R800 due to revised element insert". So DN15-R400, DN20-R400, DN15-R800, DN20-R800 seems a reasonable labeling. But maybe better to stay literal: model_id "DN15¹" with footnote_markers. Hmm, the schema allows label field. Let me do:

models: [
  {"model_id": "DN15", "label": "DN15 (element insert per doc. 12126/0-05)", "attributes": {"q3_over_q1": 400}},
  {"model_id": "DN20", "label": "DN20 (element insert per doc. 12126/0-05)", ...},
  ...
]

But model_id should be unique per variant. Two DN15 entries with same model_id is confusing. I'll use model_id: "DN15-R400", "DN20-R400", "DN15-R800", "DN20-R800" with label describing. Actually let me keep model_id as "DN15¹" etc.? JSON can hold "DN15¹". Hmm, but footnote markers shouldn't be embedded per rules... The rules say never include footnote markers in labels of characteristics. For model ids, cleaner to do "DN15 (R400)" / "DN15 (R800)".

I'll go with model_id "DN15-R400" etc., label "DN15 with element insert per documentation number 12126/0-05".

Matrix tables: Table 3 (flow characteristics by meter size) and Table 4 (indicating device) and Table 2 (software identification).

matrix_tables:
1. name: "General characteristics of the family of instruments"
   columns: ["meter_size", "q1", "q2", "q3", "q4", "q3_q1_ratio"]
   rows: 4 rows with model keys.
2. name: "Software identification"
   columns: ["product_code", "firmware_platform", "firmware_version", "checksum"]
   rows: 5 rows.
3. Table 4: name "General characteristics of the indicating device", columns: meter_size, indicating_range_minimum_value, verification_scale_interval; row: {"meter_size": "DN15; DN20", "indicating_range_minimum_value": 9999.99999, "verification_scale_interval": 0.00001}

characteristics type_level (Table 1):
- measuring_principle: "Ultrasonic"
- accuracy_class: "2"
- environmental_class: "M1 / O (installed outdoors)" — value string "M1 / O", note installed outdoors. Keep as string with the full? I'll put value "M1 / O" and maybe a separate note. Actually keep "M1 / O (installed outdoors)" as string.
- electromagnetic_environment: "E1"
- temperature_range_ambient: {min: -25, max: 55}, unit °C
- water_temperature_class: T50 (+0.1 °C / +50 °C) → water_temperature_class: "T50"; and water_temperature_range: {min: 0.1, max: 50}, unit °C. Note it's +0,1 °C meaning from +0.1 to +50. Yes.
- maximum_admissible_pressure_map: 1.6 MPa; also 16 bar. Two units. I could emit map_mpa and map_bar or one entry with value 1.6 unit MPa and note. I'll emit:
  - maximum_admissible_pressure: {value: 1.6, unit_symbol: "MPa"}
  - maximum_admissible_pressure_bar equivalent? Maybe value {min...}. Hmm. I'll add second characteristic "maximum_admissible_pressure_equivalent" value 16 unit "bar". Or keep it simple: one with value 1.6 MPa, footnote? Better: two entries: maximum_admissible_pressure (MPa) and maximum_admissible_pressure (bar)? Ambiguous names. I'll do "maximum_admissible_pressure": 1.6 MPa and "maximum_admissible_pressure_bar": 16 bar. Slightly awkward but fine. Alternatively value as string "1,6 MPa (16 bar)". Rules say separate numeric from unit. I'll go with two entries.
- orientation: "All positions (horizontal, vertical or diagonal)" — string.
- flow_profile_sensitivity_class: "U0 and D0 (0 x DN upstream and 0 x DN downstream)" — string.
- reverse_flow: "The sensor is not intended to measure reverse flow" — string.
- pressure_loss_class: "Δp 25" — value; with (0.25 bar). I'll emit pressure_loss_class: "Δp 25" and pressure_loss: {max: 0.25, unit: "bar"}. Actually "Δp 25 (0,25 bar)" means class Δp25 corresponding to max pressure loss 0.25 bar at Q3. I'll do pressure_loss_class: {"value": "Δp 25"} and pressure_loss_max: 0.25 bar.
- power_supply: battery. → power_supply_type: "Non-replaceable battery"; battery_voltage: {min: 3.2, max: 3.6, unit: "V"}; battery_life: {value: 15, unit: "years"}.
- software_identification: "See table 2" — could omit or record as string reference. I'll omit from characteristics (covered by matrix table).
- characteristics_of_indicating_device: "See table 4" — omit.

model_level characteristics:
- q1, q2, q3, q4 each with unit m³/h and 4 values.
- q3_q1_ratio: 400/400/800/800 dimensionless.

config_level: The variant axis here is element insert (footnote 1 vs 2). Is that a model or config? The models are DN15 and DN20; the axis is element insert version. I could model as model_level with 4 models (DN15¹, DN20¹, DN15², DN20²) — simpler. I'll treat 4 models.

Footnote markers on values: DN15-R400 values footnote_markers ["1)"], DN15-R800 ["2)"] etc. In matrix_tables rows too? The matrix table schema has footnotes[] field at table level. I'll add footnotes to that table: [{"marker": "1)", "text": ...}, {"marker": "2)", "text": ...}]. And global footnotes[] as well.

Table 2 rows:
- product_code 0x0700, ARM - Standard Output, F 1.0.4414, checksum "0x6A4A 68EB *"
- 0x0702, ARM - Wire M-BUS, F 1.0.548, 0xC8AD E86F *

Certificate number: "R49/2013-A-NL1-21.04". Revision 5. number field: "R49/2013-A-NL1-21.04" — include revision? The schema has number, and revision_history. I'll set number: "R49/2013-A-NL1-21.04" and maybe note revision 5. There's no revision field at certificate level except revision_history. The date_issued: 31 August 2026 → ISO "2026-08-31".

oiml_issuer_id: "NL1".

page_total: 4.

Category: "Water meter". The schema category examples: "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system", "Fuel dispenser", "Taximeter", "Gas meter"... So "Water meter".

Components: not named as sub-assemblies explicitly, other than "measurement sensor with element insert" and "indicating device". Should I add components? The cert mentions the measurement sensor and indicating device (Table 4). It's borderline. I could add components: measuring sensor (with element inserts), indicating device, calculating device? Not explicitly named as separate. I'll skip components to avoid fabrication, but Table 4 covers indicating device characteristics. Actually maybe include component "measurement sensor" role with the element insert documentation numbers? Hmm. Rule 6: include ONLY if cert names sub-assemblies.
